title: Suspicious Network Activity Investigation
briefing: Unusual outbound traffic and irregular connection patterns have been detected from an internal system. The security team must determine whether this is benign noise, misconfiguration, or signs of active compromise.

injects.title: Threat Intelligence Correlation
injects.message: Threat intelligence feeds report similar outbound traffic patterns associated with recently observed command-and-control infrastructure.

injects.title: Additional Suspicious Traffic Detected
injects.message: Monitoring tools begin flagging similar outbound traffic patterns from another internal system, suggesting the activity may not be isolated.

injects.title: Executive Visibility
injects.message: Leadership becomes aware of the investigation and asks whether additional systems may need monitoring or containment measures.

injects.title: Account Abuse Concern
injects.message: Identity monitoring systems flag unusual login activity associated with the same system involved in the network anomaly.

step_1.situation: Monitoring tools detect unusual outbound traffic from an internal host outside expected business hours. The team begins by identifying the most important risk indicators.

if_correct.consequence: The team correctly identifies the major warning signs and treats the activity as a potentially meaningful security event.

if_incorrect.consequence: The event is treated as a minor anomaly, delaying containment and allowing suspicious activity to continue.

step_2.situation: Security reviews whether network controls, segmentation, and boundary protections can reduce exposure while the host is investigated.

if_correct.consequence: Containment actions reduce the chance of additional outbound communication and help narrow the scope of analysis.

if_incorrect.consequence: Weak containment planning leaves the environment exposed to continued suspicious traffic and possible expansion.

step_3.situation: Leadership asks for an immediate answer: is this harmless, policy-related, or evidence of active compromise requiring escalation?

if_correct.consequence: A timely and structured response improves confidence while preserving room for deeper technical review.

if_incorrect.consequence: Slow or unclear communication creates confusion and increases pressure on the response team.

step_4.situation: The team considers whether identity controls and account protections reduce the likelihood that suspicious network activity is tied to broader account abuse.

if_correct.consequence: Stronger identity controls help narrow the risk picture and reduce the likelihood of uncontrolled access expansion.

if_incorrect.consequence: Weak assumptions about access controls make it harder to distinguish isolated activity from broader compromise.

step_5.situation: Business stakeholders begin asking whether staff should be notified and whether operations may be affected if network restrictions expand.

if_correct.consequence: Communication remains measured and credible, helping preserve trust while the investigation continues.

if_incorrect.consequence: Poor stakeholder communication increases uncertainty and complicates the response environment.
